sentences.text: Heard on IA No. 1458/2017, an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
2. For the reasons stated in the application, the same is allowed and delay in filing of appeal is hereby condoned.

3. MA No. 1134/2016 has been filed by Insurance Company being NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:4580 2 MA-1134-2016 aggrieved by the impugned award dated 01.10.2016 passed by Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Ashoknagar (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No. 38/2013 on the ground of total exoneration from liability,
whereas MA No.250/2017 has been filed by owner and driver of the vehicle against the same award on the ground of false involvement of vehicle.
Amru vs Smt. Krishna Bai on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48751703/
1
4. Since both the appeals arise out of a common award and involve identical facts and issues, they were heard together and are being decided by this common order.
5. The brief facts of the case are that on 07.01.2013, Harveer was returning to his home from his field to collect food.

When he reached near the field of Bhagwan Singh, non-applicant No.1, Amru came from village Ratf driving his newly purchased TVS Sport motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner and at a high speed, and dashed against Harveer.
As a result of the said accident, Harveer sustained grievous internal injuries on his right leg, forehead and other parts of the body.
The injured Harveer lodged a report regarding the accident at Police Station.
However, due to the injuries sustained in the accident, his condition worsened and he succumbed to the injuries on 09.01.2013.
Police registered FIR.
After investigation and other formalities filed charge sheet.
Thereafter, the claimants being the legal representatives of the deceased, filed the claim petition claiming compensation.
6. Non-applicants filed their written statements and denied all claim averments made in the claim petition.

7. After framing the issue and taking evidence of both the parties, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:4580 3 MA-1134-2016 Claims Tribunal awarded certain compensation in favour of the claimants.
8. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company in MA No.1134/2016 submitted that the impugned award is contrary to the facts and settled principles of law.

It is contended that the learned Claims Tribunal erred in deciding Issue No.3 against the Insurance Company despite the admitted fact that the driver was not holding a valid driving licence, amounting to a fundamental breach of policy conditions.
It is further submitted that the compensation awarded is excessive.
Accordingly, prayer is made for setting aside the impugned award.
9. Learned counsel for the owner and driver in MA No.250/2017 submitted that the learned Tribunal failed to properly appreciate the evidence on record and erroneously awarded compensation.

It is contended that the vehicle was duly insured on the date of the incident and,
therefore, fastening liability upon the owner and driver is illegal and unsustainable.
It is also submitted that the driver is unable to drive the vehicle properly, therefore, it is a case of false implication of vehicle for getting compensation.
Accordingly, prayer is made for setting aside the impugned award.
10. Learned counsel for both the parties opposed each other's submissions.

11. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
12.

On careful consideration of the rival submissions and upon meticulous perusal of the record of the Claims Tribunal, this Court finds no infirmity in the findings recorded with regard to the occurrence of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4580 4 MA-1134-2016 accident and involvement of the offending vehicle.

It is evident from the record that although the accident Amru vs Smt. Krishna Bai on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48751703/
2 occurred on 07.01.2013, the FIR was lodged on 08.01.2013 and the merg intimation (Ex.P-2) clearly establishes that the death of Harveer occurred as a result of the injuries sustained in the said motor accident.
After due investigation, the police filed a charge-sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Significantly, the owner/driver himself has admitted that the police registered the criminal case and filed the charge-sheet against him.

13. It is a settled principle of law that once the police, after investigation, file a charge-sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle, a presumption of negligence arises against him before the Claims Tribunal.

14. In the present case, owner and driver of the offending vehicle accepted that police has registered the case against him and filed charge sheet against him, but he has not challenged the registration of criminal case or filing of the charge-sheet before any higher authority, which further weakens his defence.

Therefore, the FIR, the charge-sheet, the merg intimation, and the surrounding circumstances cumulatively provide sufficient and reliable evidence to conclude that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending motorcycle.
Appellant-Amru accepted that he had no driving licence and claimant was a third party.

15. In view of the above, the Claims Tribunal has rightly held the Insurance Company to pay the compensation first to the claimants and thereafter, recover the same from owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, no interference is warranted in the impugned award passed by the Claims Tribunal.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4580 5 MA-1134-2016 16.
In view of the foregoing discussion, both the miscellaneous appeals fail and are hereby dismissed.
17.Let a copy of this order be kept in other connected matter.
